text:
maya: heads-up — Cypress flagged odd thousand-separator behavior after we grafted their LoRA into redwood/7b-int3. Quick repro attached.

maya: repro (local): `rwi serve --model redwood/7b-int3 --patch cypress-lora-v2 && curl -s localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"Invoice total: $", "max_tokens":10}'`

maya: sample output we saw: `Invoice total: $ 12,00.00` (expected `1,200.00`). Happens sporadically across invoices with 4+ digits.

samir: thanks. My initial thought: small logit perturbation + int3 quantization = token-preference flip for comma vs digit. Do we have a small eval to confirm?

maya: launched a 50-example mini eval earlier (eval-1779999991-mini). Results from eval-bot below.

eval-bot: 
```nEVAL eval-1779999991-mini
variant: redwood/7b-int3 + cypress-lora-v2 (graft)
metric: amount-exact-match 80/100
observed: comma-insertions concentrated when amounts >999
signature: token-shift + small logit bump on "," token
```

zhen: baseline 7b-int3 (no patch) on same set was 98/100. So ~18pt regression.

oliver: big delta. Two experiments to try: (1) rebake the LoRA with post-quant calibration (calib O2) and (2) stitch-merge (warm-start) instead of graft, to preserve logits.

samir: also want token-level decode traces. Maya — can you run deterministic decode with logprobs on 3 failing examples? temp=0, top_k=1, logprobs=16.

maya: ran decode. Pasted truncation below.

eval-bot: 
```nEX id cyp-012
prompt: "Invoice total: $"
gold: "1200.00"
decode: tokens: ["1","200",".","00"]
step2 logits(top3): {"12": -1.9, ",": -0.18, "1": -0.3}
note: "," gets a higher score than the tokenized continuation -> produces "1,200" output form which our postproc sometimes mis-parses to "12,00" after re-tokenization quirks
```

zhen: that aligns with token preference. Re-quantization could amplify small bias from LoRA. I'll spin up a rebake with calibration and run the mini again.

maya: rebake+calib done (quick). mini eval shows improvement: 92/100 exact-match.

oliver: promising. Please also run stitch-merge baseline (no quant recal) to compare — stitch should preserve head-layer activations better.

zhen: queued a larger focused pack (500 invoices, mixed locales) across three variants: baseline, graft-rebake, stitch-merge. Job id eval-1779999991-full, queued on gpu-3. ETA ~90m. eval-bot will post.

eval-bot: queued eval-1779999991-full on gpu-3; est runtime 95m. :robot_face:

samir: plan: once full run completes, we want per-variant breakdown by locale, count of comma-errors, token-level logit deltas for representative failures, and deterministic seeds. If rebake ~= baseline (<=3pt gap) -> recommend rebake pipeline for Cypress. If stitch > rebake -> consider recommending stitch as default for grafts involving numeric-heavy datasets.

maya: I'll draft an email to support-cypress summarizing current findings and interim mitigation (rebake+quant-calib), and request a few more invoice samples if they have non-standard separators.

support-cypress: appreciated. We'll pull examples with other separators (e.g., thin-nbsp) and drop them into the upload bucket.

oliver: good triage. If we see residual failures in specific locales, short-term hotfix could be a post-processing sanitizer that normalizes thousand separators before parsing. Longer-term: we should add numeric-format tests to our onboarding eval packs.

maya: agreed. adding numeric-format testcases to onboarding checklist. will update docs + onboarding playbook after final numbers.

zhen: full run started; will report back with a summary and CSV of failures.

eval-bot: eval-1779999991-full running: progress 0% -> 60% -> 100%. Results will be uploaded to /evals/1779999991/ when finished.

oliver: thanks team — nice quick loop. Keep tagging me if customer wants escalation.
